items.name: Peach Cobbler Loaf
ingredients: 1¼ pounds (565 grams) peaches, pitted (no need to peel); each peach cut into 8 wedges
Finely grated zest and juice from half a lemon
⅓ cup (72 grams) plus 1 tablespoon (15 grams) light brown sugar, divided
6 tablespoons (3 ounces or 85 grams) unsalted butter, cold is fine
½ cup (115 grams) plain unsweetened Greek-style yogurt or sour cream
2 tablespoons (30 grams) unsalted butter, cold is fine
steps: Heat oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a loaf pan (see Note up top about size) with parchment paper — I like to extend it up two sides and spray any unlined part of the pan with nonstick spray. Place on a larger sheet pan just in case there are drips.

Prepare the cake: Finely grate the lemon zest into a large bowl and set aside. Place peach wedges in a medium bowl and squeeze the juice of the lemon half over it. Add cinnamon and 1 tablespoon of the brown sugar and stir to coat. Set aside.

Add 6 tablespoons melted butter to the larger bowl (with the zest in it), along with granulated sugar (⅓ cup) and remaining (⅓ cup) brown sugar; whisk to combine. Add yogurt or sour cream and mix. Add eggs and beat to combine.

Sprinkle the surface of the batter with baking powder, baking soda, and salt and whisk thoroughly to combine, giving it a few extra stirs to make sure it’s mixed well. Add the flour (1⅓ cups) and stir until it disappears.
Make the streusel: Melt remaining 2 tablespoons butter in a small bowl. Stir in remaining granulated sugar (2 tablespoons) and pinch of salt, then remaining flour (¼ cup) until crumbs form.

Assemble the cake: Pour half of cake batter in your prepared pan, spreading it evenly. Arrange half of peaches on the batter in one layer. Spoon remaining batter over and spread it evenly. Arrange remaining peaches on top of the batter, then pour any juices collected in the bowl over the peaches. Sprinkle peaches with streusel.

Bake the cake: Place your prepared pan on a baking sheet (if you ignored me the first time, as I would have) and bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until a tester inserted into the center of the cake and also a few times under the top peach layer (where unbaked batter likes to collect) comes out clean. It might need up to 5 minutes longer. Let cool on a rack.
To serve: Run a knife along any sides of the cake that aren’t lined with parchment and use the parchment paper to lift it out of the loaf pan. Cut into thick slices.

Do ahead: This cake is very good on the first day but honestly even better on the second and third, if you’re planning ahead. I store it in the pan at room temperature, unwrapped (but often tuck it inside the microwave or oven as a kind of makeshift bread box) because I want the top to keep its texture.

items.name: Peanut Chicken with Ginger Slaw
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, thinly sliced
¼ cup Trader Joe’s Peanut Satay Sauce (more for serving)
1 clove garlic, grated (or ½ teaspoon garlic powder)
1 tablespoon ginger paste (or grated fresh ginger)
4–5 cups shredded purple cabbage, very thinly sliced on a mandoline (about half of a head of cabbage)
1 shallot, very thinly sliced on a mandoline (optional, but I like it in there!)
steps: Prep Chicken: Mix the chicken with peanut sauce, garlic, and salt. Let it rest for 15-30 minutes while you prep the other ingredients.

Coconut Rice: Rinse the rice under cold running water. Add to a saucepan with water, coconut milk, and salt; bring to a low simmer. Cover with a lid, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove lid; fluff rice with a fork.
Ginger Slaw: Stir the vinegar, sugar, ginger, and salt together in a large bowl. Add shredded cabbage and shallots; massage with your hands for a few minutes to tenderize the cabbage.
Cook Chicken: Heat the avocado oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium high heat. Add the chicken and stir fry, moving around in the pan to prevent burning, for a few minutes until fully cooked.

Serve: Place the coconut rice in a bowl, top with peanut chicken, and pile that slaw on top. Spoon extra peanut sauce over the chicken. Add cilantro, crispy shallots, and/or chili crisp to finish it off!

items.name: Honey BBQ Chicken Bites
ingredients: 1 ½ pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs cut into 1-inch chunks
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Coat a cooling rack with nonstick spray and place on a baking sheet; set aside.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, BBQ seasoning, ½ teaspoon salt and ½teaspoon pepper.
In a medium bowl, whisk together buttermilk and egg.
In a large bowl, combine cornflake crumbs and vegetable oil; season with salt and pepper, to taste.
Working one at a time, dredge chicken in flour, dip into buttermilk mixture, then dredge in cornflakes mixture, pressing to coat.
Place chicken in a single layer onto the prepared baking sheet and coat with nonstick spray.
Place into oven and bake until crisp and cooked through, about 15-18 minutes.
In a large bowl, gently combine chicken and ½ the honey BBQ sauce.
Serve immediately with the remaining honey BBQ sauce.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, combine BBQ sauce, honey, apple cider vinegar and hot sauce, if using, until warmed through, about 2-3 minutes.

items.name: Teriyaki Chicken with Ginger Peaches and Sesame Drench
ingredients: ½ cup teriyaki sauce (I use Soy Vay)
1 large clove garlic, grated (or ½ teaspoon garlic powder)
¼ cup chopped scallions, or cilantro, or both
1–2 tablespoons water (as needed, to thin it out)
steps: Prep Chicken: Slice the chicken breast into thinner pieces, or pound them out to be thinner.
Marinate Chicken: Marinate the chicken in the sauce and garlic for 2-12 hours. (Optional – more time = better flavor, but it will work even with a shorter 15-30 minute marinate time!)
Make Rice: Start cooking your rice according to package directions.
Make Sauce: Whisk the sesame drench ingredients together and set aside.

Make Gingery Peaches: When you’re close to being ready to eat, toss peaches, scallions, ginger, salt, and sugar together. Usually the peaches will release some juices and it will become slightly saucy, but you can add a bit of honey to help it along if it seems too dry.

Cook Chicken: Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Let any excess marinade drip off the chicken, then add to the pan and sauté for 3-4 minutes per side, until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165 degrees.
Serve: Serve the chicken over rice, with a scoop of the peaches, and a drench of the sesame sauce! Add green beans if you’d like! So super fresh!
